# Protein structure {#sec-protein-structure}

::: {.callout-note title="From the exam description"}
Knowledge of protein structure including domains and different methods to
predict protein structure.
:::

## Introduction

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Short introduction: the protein folding problem (Anfinsen, Levinthal);
secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure; domains and folds;
experimental structure determination; the path from secondary structure
prediction through homology modelling, fold recognition, fragment assembly
and coevolution to AlphaFold; membrane proteins; design and docking.
:::

## Key concepts

- Levels of protein structure; packing of helices and sheets; domains, folds, superfamilies
- Anfinsen's dogma and Levinthal's paradox
- Experimental methods: X-ray crystallography (R-free), NMR, cryo-EM; resolution and model quality
- Structure comparison: RMSD, TM-score, structural alignment (DALI, TM-align)
- Secondary structure prediction: Chou–Fasman, GOR, neural networks with profiles (PHD, PSIPRED)
- Homology (comparative) modelling: template selection, alignment, MODELLER
- Fold recognition/threading: 3D profiles, threading potentials, profile–profile methods
- De novo prediction: fragment assembly (Rosetta), energy functions, sampling
- Coevolution: direct-coupling analysis, contact prediction, deep-learning contact maps
- AlphaFold2 (MSA + attention, structure module, pLDDT, PAE), RoseTTAFold, protein language models (ESMFold), AlphaFold3
- Evaluation: CASP and its metrics (GDT_TS, lDDT)
- Membrane proteins: hydrophobicity, positive-inside rule, topology prediction (TMHMM, DeepTMHMM)
- Molecular dynamics (principles); docking and scoring functions
- Protein design: from Dahiyat & Mayo to Rosetta, ProteinMPNN and RFdiffusion

## Key papers

::: {.callout-tip}
★ = mandatory in earlier reading lists.
:::

### Fundamentals

- @anfinsen1973 — principles that govern the folding of protein chains.
- @levinthal1966 — molecular model-building by computer.
- @chothia1977 — packing of α-helices and β-sheets.
- @holm1996 — mapping the protein universe.

### Domains and classification

See also the structure classification papers in @sec-databases.

- @reeves2006 — structural diversity of domain superfamilies in CATH.
- @zhang2005 — TM-align: structural alignment with TM-score.

### Experimental structure determination

- @brunger1992 — the free R value.
- @scheres2012 — a Bayesian view on cryo-EM structure determination.

### Secondary structure prediction

- @chou1974a, @chou1974b — Chou–Fasman parameters and prediction.
- @garnier1978 — GOR: information-theoretic prediction.
- ★ @rost1993 — PHD: profiles + neural networks, >70% accuracy.
- @jones1999 — PSIPRED: prediction based on position-specific scoring matrices.

### Homology modelling and fold recognition

- ★ @sali1993 — MODELLER: comparative modelling by satisfaction of spatial restraints.
- @bowie1991 — 3D profiles: identifying sequences that fit a known structure.
- @jones1992 — threading: a new approach to fold recognition.
- @fischer1996 — fold recognition using sequence-derived predictions.

### De novo prediction and coevolution

- @simons1997 — Rosetta fragment assembly.
- ★ @bradley2005 — high-resolution de novo prediction for small proteins.
- @weigt2009 — direct coupling analysis of residue contacts.
- @marks2011 — 3D structure computed from evolutionary sequence variation.
- ★ @marks2012 — review: protein structure prediction from sequence variation.
- ★ @wang2017 — RaptorX: contact prediction with ultra-deep learning.

### Deep-learning structure prediction

- @senior2020 — AlphaFold (CASP13).
- @jumper2021 — AlphaFold2.
- @baek2021 — RoseTTAFold.
- @lin2023 — ESMFold: structure prediction from a language model.
- @abramson2024 — AlphaFold3: complexes with proteins, nucleic acids and ligands.
- @kryshtafovych2021 — CASP14 assessment.

### Membrane proteins

- ★ @vonheijne1992 — hydrophobicity analysis and the positive-inside rule.
- @krogh2001 — TMHMM: topology prediction with a hidden Markov model.
- @elofsson2007 — membrane protein structure: prediction versus reality.
- @hallgren2022 — DeepTMHMM.

### Molecular dynamics and docking

- @mccammon1977 — the first MD simulation of a protein.
- @kuntz1982 — a geometric approach to macromolecule–ligand interactions (DOCK).
- @meng1992 — grid-based docking.
- @bohm1994 — an empirical scoring function for binding affinity.
- ★ @muegge1999 — a knowledge-based scoring function (PMF).
- @warren2006 — a critical assessment of docking programs and scoring functions.

### Protein design

- @dahiyat1997 — fully automated de novo design.
- @jiang2008 — computational design of retro-aldol enzymes.
- @koga2012 — principles for designing ideal protein structures.
- ★ @huang2016 — the coming of age of de novo protein design.
- @dauparas2022 — ProteinMPNN: deep-learning sequence design.
- @watson2023 — RFdiffusion: de novo design with diffusion models.
